note: 25 sheets, and the running folio 'Page N of 25' matches the sheet index on every sheet that prints one. Ten figures and two tables survive measurement, plus 26 excluded regions. The paper prints exactly ONE numbered exhibit caption in its whole run - 'Figure 2: Generating and Restricting Relationship' on p11, set above the art and sharing its baseline with the watermark glyph run so the text layer reads '...MATHmodels Figure 2: Generating and Restricting Relationship'. There is no Figure 1 anywhere, no Figure 3 to follow it, and no table number at all: the other nine measured figures carry their titles baked into the raster ('Elbow Method with Optimal K=5 for Five Elements Theory', 'PCA of Data Before Clustering' / 'PCA of Data with Adjusted K-means Clustering (5 Clusters)', 'Cybersecurity Threat Clustering Analysis Based on Five Elements Theory', 'Policy Effect Comparison among Countries/Regions', 'Policy Score vs. Cybercrime Rate', 'Policy Impact Map: Effectiveness in Reducing Cybercrime', the three 'Sensitivity Analysis' strips), one carries a text-layer title instead (the SEM schematic on p22) and one - the five-node cycle on the Memo sheet - carries no title at all. Four page-size facts matter for reading the rest: sheet 1 is a letter-size Summary page, 612x792, while every other sheet is A4 595.3x841.9; five sheets are 0.3 by 0.9 points smaller still, 595x841, and those five are flat pasted rasters with no text layer, no images and no drawings - p2 (the tail of the contents list), p3 (the contents tail plus section 1 and the world map), p4 (section 1.1-1.2), p17 (the body of 5.3.3) and p18 (sections 6, 6.1, 6.2 and the softmax equation). The paper also types EVERY formula as a picture - 16 of them, from the z-score on p6 through the K-means trio on p7, the six weighted-Gower and regularisation formulas on p13, the three association/constraint/integer-programming formulas on p14 and one each on p15, p19 and p20 - so the layout pass sees 16 small rasters in the prose flow that are not exhibits and are excluded as such. Declared gaps: the world choropleth titled 'Global Cybersecurity Level Evaluation (2020)' with its 'Cybersecurity Level' colour bar 0-100, which is printed on the zero-text sheet 3 and cannot be measured; and any exhibit that 6.4 promised but never printed - the section lists three visualization methods, 'Policy Influence Map', 'Interaction Effect Diagram' and 'Text Clustering Visualization', and only the first reaches paper (p20, and there titled 'Policy Impact Map'). A third gap is a reference to art that does not exist: p4 says 'we have created a visual guide showcasing our workflow, as depicted in Figure 2', but the only Figure 2 printed in the file is the five-elements wheel on p11, so the workflow diagram is cited and never drawn - and the p4 citation itself is invisible to the text layer because it sits on a zero-text sheet. Two colour bars exist and neither belongs to a numbered figure: the 'Cluster' ramp 0.0-4.0 on the right-hand PCA card (p9) and the 'Effectiveness' ramp 0-1 on the policy choropleth (p20); a third would have been the one on the unmeasurable p3 map. No figure is three-dimensional and no figure prints a value on its marks. Panel structure: the PCA pair on p9 is two cards side by side with no letters; the sensitivity exhibit on p23 is three stacked graphs that the detector cuts into two regions, one full-width panel over two side-by-side panels, so it is recorded as one row plus one fragment-of-other. Nine identical watermark QR blocks are excluded at 693 paths in the box 450-590 by 767-837 (p6, p8, p10, p12, p14, p16, p20, p22, p24); the same block on p7 is a raster at the foot of the sheet, returns no region and needs no exclusion, and its glyphs reach the text layer as a band of 'm' characters. Finally the two measured tables sit at opposite ends of the paper's habits: the '3 Notations' glossary on p5 is the only grid the detector reads as a grid (three rules, no verticals, text_inside), while the Memo's policy table on p25 is a fully boxed three-column grid with two full-height vertical rules that survives only as a raster.
